thread:
lia: FYI — noticed a recurring host-side p99 blip correlated with kernel rebinds + a flurry of tiny HTTP/2 DATA frames after rolling traffic. Dumped quick traces.

lia: short summary: p99 decode jumps ~3x for a ~15min window at rotate; heap & cpu samples point at parse + convert paths allocating many small buffers.

matt: can you paste the top heap/cpu snippets?

lia: cpu samples (aggregated):
```
Total: 480ms
 160ms 33.3% host::request_parser
 120ms 25.0% kvcache::materialize_layout
 80ms 16.7% runtime.mallocgc
 40ms 8.3% tokenizer::emit_slices
 80ms 16.7% other
```

lia: heap: lots of tiny Vecs from parse + serde and extra allocation during kvcache conversion. Also saw many GRPC writev calls with small iovecs.

sam: hypothesis: kernel-selector is switching kernels per-request (AKS) and some kernels require a different KV layout. When that happens we convert/serialize on the host and malloc churns. Mix of small frames makes conversion cost dominate.

ryan: we also saw many new streams around the roll time; TLS handshakes + new connections -> more small HEADERS/DATA sequences. That amplifies the tiny-write pattern.

lia: packet sketch from tcpdump at the window:
```
02:14:03.122 -> HEADERS(48B)
02:14:03.128 -> DATA(64B)
02:14:03.131 -> DATA(96B)
02:14:03.139 -> DATA(40B)
```

jas: immediate mitigations?

sam: short list: 
- ingress coalesce: group tiny frames for 50-200ms windows and parse once
- slab allocator: thread-local bump for parse/serde scratch buffers to avoid GC churn
- kernel stickiness: prefer stable kernel per ingress-client to avoid layout conversions
- kvcache: support multi-layout entries so conversion is lazy or cached

matt: I can spike a thread-local arena for parse buffers. Will keep fallback to heap for large blobs. Also add metrics (arena_reuse, arena_bytes).

lia: I prototyped a small coalescer in the edge proxy: 100ms window + size cap 8KB. Microbench (mixed tiny+tail): p99 improved 3.5x and allocs down ~70%.

ryan: good. But we should be cautious with latency-sensitive flows; coalescing adds tail latency for small requests. Maybe make it opt-in per route and only for streaming endpoints that tolerate a small batching window.

sam: agreed. Add route-level config: coalesce_ms + max_bytes. Default disabled for payment/auth routes.

lia: the tricky part: kernel-selector (AKS) is currently per-pod and reactive to seq distribution. That causes inconsistency across replicas. If ingress routes some traffic to a pod with different kernel, we trigger conversions. Suggest making AKS sticky per client or pin kernel per ingress shard for at least N minutes.

jas: doing stickiness reduces conversions but may reduce kernel efficiency for sudden distribution shifts. We can add a warm-up window for new kernels before full traffic is routed.

matt: prototype notes for slab allocator:
- use thread_local Vec<u8> with bump pointer and epoch counter
- max slab size 64KB, slices returned as &mut [u8] with lifetime tied to request; on coroutine yield ensure slab has reserved space or fallback to heap
- instrument with slab_allocs, slab_fallbacks

sam: important: ensure slab buffers are zeroed only if kernel conversion requires zeroed alignment; otherwise we can skip memzero to save cycles. Also keep an aligned-return helper for AVX-friendly layouts.

lia: I opened a PR for the coalescer on the ingress-proxy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/239 — feature-flagged, metrics added (coalesce_windows, coalesce_dropped).

matt: slab PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4811 — behind feature flag, includes tokio-yield safety tests and perf counters.

lia: perf-bot: quick CI bench after enabling slab + coalesce in local canary.

perf-bot: bench-suite: mixed-streaming: p50/p95/p99 baseline=6ms/48ms/210ms -> coalesce+slab=6ms/28ms/64ms; heap allocs -68%.

ryan: ops note: also toggle gRPC keepalive and connection reuse to reduce new TLS streams on roll. Ops will enable keepalives for canary.

jas: longer-term: update kvcache metadata to store layout-variants and last-conversion timestamp; that way we avoid repeated conversions and can prewarm common layouts. RFC in flight.

lia: rollout plan:
1) enable ingress coalesce (route opt-in) on canary today
2) deploy slab behind flag on runtime canaries tomorrow and enable for streaming routes
3) if stable 48h, enable kernel stickiness or AKS warm-up and re-enable AKS progressively

sam: add alert: kvcache_conversion_rate > 100/min AND kvcache_miss_rate > 10% -> paging-list. Also dashboard tiles for slab_fallbacks and coalesce_latency.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: ingress-proxy coalesce flag enabled on canary at 2026-03-09T02:30:12Z

lia: thanks team — will follow up with soak results.
